Mulled Dry Cider for Candlemas

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 4-6Prep 5 minCook 20-25 min

On Candlemas, February 2nd, traditions often include enjoying crepes, especially in France. A perfect accompaniment to these delicate pancakes, or simply a warming treat for a cold winter's day, is a fragrant mulled dry cider. This recipe elevates a simple purchased dry cider into a comforting, spiced beverage, ideal for sharing during this festive and reflective holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 gallon (about 1.9 liters) dry apple cider (hard cider, not apple juice)
  • 2 cinnamon sticks
  • 1 teaspoon whole cloves
  • 2-3 star anise pods
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh orange juice (from about 1/2 orange)
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) maple syrup or honey, or to taste (optional)
  • Orange slices, for garnish (optional)
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) brandy or Calvados (optional, for an adult version)

Method

  1. Pour the dry apple cider into a large saucepan or pot.
  2. Add the cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, star anise pods, and fresh orange juice to the cider. If using, add maple syrup or honey now.
  3. Heat the mixture over medium heat, bringing it to a gentle simmer. Do not boil, as boiling can cause the alcohol to evaporate and can diminish the delicate flavors of the spices.
  4. Reduce the heat to low and let the cider gently simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and deepen.
  5. Taste the mulled cider and adjust sweetness if desired, adding more maple syrup or honey if preferred.
  6. If making an adult version, stir in the brandy or Calvados just before serving.
  7. Strain the cider through a fine-mesh sieve to remove the whole spices, or leave them in for presentation.
  8. Ladle the warm mulled cider into heatproof mugs or glasses. Garnish each serving with an orange slice, if desired.

Tips

  • For a spicier kick, add a few slices of fresh ginger or a pinch of ground nutmeg to the simmering cider.
  • If you prefer a less dry cider, you can use a semi-dry or even a traditional hard cider and adjust the sweetener accordingly.
  • Leftover mulled cider can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and gently reheated on the stovetop or in the microwave.
